messages.author: 8b1d44188d548e05
messages.subject: Data preparation
parts:
Hi again Chris,

I previously asked about unit calibration and in the conversation you brought up some other issues that I had with my time stamp column and perhaps not prepping my data in excel/csv. I was wondering if you could give me some advice on how to prep my raw data into something that is usable by the ctmm package (I know it follows the move bank format, I just do not know the best way to go about this). I am attaching my raw data from one GPS unit (this was actually tracking cows, not just for calibration). This data is pilot data and will kind of be a mess because I need to delete rows where they were stationary in a pen and rows when they were moved to another pasture, but I am wondering if you could help on: which columns I need to keep and can be used by the package, how to efficiently make a timestamp column (times are not adjusted for PST (GMT-8) in the raw data).

Thank you so much for all of your help!

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Data preparation
parts:
Hi,

It looks like you just need a timestamp column, which would combine the date and time columns, and then you will probably need to supply a timeformat argument. Beyond that, you might want to try naming EHPE to HDOP, to see if that works as a relative measure of error, and perhaps looking if there is any association between error and Timeout.

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: Re: Data preparation
parts:
Hi Maggie,

You don't need to delete columns unless they have deceptive names, which I didn't see. MoveBank attribute names should always work, but I try to code everything variation that I see. "longitude" is fine.

Best,
Chris
